design_intent: Open hardware portrait smartphone-like single board for projects that need an all-in-one touch-display USB-C receptacle device with TROPIC01 as the mandatory open secure element/root of trust.

host_controller_decision.recommended_host: STM32U5 family, preferably STM32U585VIT6 in LQFP100 for Rev A0, with STM32U575VIT6 as fallback if sourcing or firmware constraints require it.
host_controller_decision.decision: STM32U5 is the default host MCU for the universal reference board. ESP32-S3 and radio-capable MCUs are not part of the single product because radios add unnecessary default attack surface.
host_controller_decision.rationale: The reference board should minimize default attack surface, keep always-on radios absent from the core assembly, provide TrustZone-class isolation, support secure boot and debug lock, expose USB and display workflows, and stay close to the architecture lessons from Trezor Safe 7 and the official Tropic USB DevKit host pattern.
host_controller_decision.package_policy: Rev A0 should use LQFP100 unless pin-mux review proves it too tight. LQFP144 is the expansion fallback. BGA is deferred until after Rev A0 pinout, DFM, test jig, and assembly yield are proven.

mechanical_decision.shape: Portrait smartphone-like rectangle. The board follows the selected touch-display module envelope instead of adding large unused wings.
mechanical_decision.usb: USB-C receptacle only. A USB-C plug version is deferred because it creates mechanical stress, host-device ambiguity, enclosure constraints, and a worse reference-platform story.
mechanical_decision.placement: USB-C receptacle on the bottom short edge, NFC antenna zone on the top short edge, and two side buttons high on the left and right long edges.
mechanical_decision.pogo: Hidden back-side pogo/test pads are covered by the enclosure in the product and do not require user-accessible case openings.
mechanical_decision.single_board_policy: The default hardware is one compact single board with display mounted above the PCB. Daughterboards are allowed only for future profile-specific accessories.

display_decision.primary_display: EastRising ER-TFT024IPS-3 portrait touch display, 2.4 inch, 240x320 IPS TFT, ST7789V display controller, FT6336 capacitive touch controller, display and touch on a single 50-pin FFC.
display_decision.minimum_display_requirement: The integrated touch display must be large enough for transaction/event review, credential review, key identity display, device status, QR rendering, and developer diagnostics.
display_decision.approval_policy: Touch is the default navigation surface, but two high side physical buttons remain the production approval/reject boundary unless a later security review accepts touch-only confirmation.
display_decision.bus_policy: The display SPI bus must remain separate from the TROPIC01 SPI bus in Rev A0.

rev_a0_component_decisions.tropic01_firmware_target: Application firmware compatibility managed through libtropic 4.0.0.
rev_a0_component_decisions.display_primary: EastRising ER-TFT024IPS-3 2.4 inch portrait 240x320 IPS TFT with ST7789V display controller and FT6336 capacitive touch controller.
rev_a0_component_decisions.display_connectors: Single 50-pin 0.5mm FFC (Hirose FH12-50S-0.5SH class) carrying both display SPI and capacitive-touch I2C; no separate touch connector.
rev_a0_component_decisions.power_primary: TPS62840DLCR 3.3 V system buck regulator, TPS22917DBVR TROPIC01 load switch, and BQ24074RGTR LiPo charger with real power-path/load-sharing for USB-or-battery operation.
rev_a0_component_decisions.storage_primary: Winbond W25Q128JVSIQ 128 Mbit QSPI NOR in SOIC-8 for Rev A0 inspectability.
rev_a0_component_decisions.second_secure_element: Infineon OPTIGA Trust M family, BOM MPN OPTIGA-TRUST-M-SLS32AIA, I2C secure element used as the independent defense-in-depth trust anchor.
rev_a0_component_decisions.removable_storage_policy: no microSD slot; do not include microSD in the single product. Use soldered QSPI flash plus USB, NFC, QR/display, or host workflows for import/export.
rev_a0_component_decisions.nfc_primary: ST25R3916B-AQET NFC controller with TPS22917DBVR power gate, 27.12 MHz crystal, top-short-edge antenna path, and disabled-by-default firmware policy.
rev_a0_component_decisions.usb_connector: GCT USB4105-GF-A female USB-C receptacle only; no plug-style default board.
rev_a0_component_decisions.side_buttons: Panasonic EVQP7J01P side-operation tactile switches for the high left/right physical approve/reject controls.

board_profiles.name: single_product
mounted: OPTIGA Trust M class I2C second secure element
female USB-C receptacle on the bottom short edge
portrait touch display mounted over the board
left and right high side buttons for physical approve/reject
power-gated NFC controller and top short edge antenna path
LiPo battery connector plus LiPo charger/power-path
hidden back-side pogo/test pads covered by the enclosure

security_requirements: TROPIC01 is mandatory and is the board root of trust for secure channel, TRNG, device authenticity evidence, pairing-key lifecycle, secure storage helpers, counters, MAC-and-Destroy, and key wrapping or unlock material.

TROPIC01 must use 3.3 V SPI with manual chip select, GPO/IRQ support where applicable, polling fallback, local decoupling, reference pull network, and test access suitable for bring-up but lockable in hardened use.
TROPIC01 reset/recovery must use a controlled power-cycle path through a load switch or equivalent power-gating circuit, not an assumed dedicated reset pin.
TR01-C2P-T301 is the default available TROPIC01 part for Rev A0, while TR01-C2P-T310 is preferred when obtainable.
Provisioning must treat the default/factory TROPIC01 pairing key as temporary and maintenance mode must be disabled after update or provisioning before hardened claims.

The 2026-06-03 TROPIC01 laser fault injection advisory must be documented for hardened profiles; board-level security must use defense in depth and maintenance-mode discipline rather than relying on a single chip.
The OPTIGA second secure element provides independent defense in depth for attestation and anti-clone policy while TROPIC01 remains the open primary secure element.
NFC is core hardware but must be power-gated and firmware-disabled by default in hardened builds.

The host MCU must support signed firmware, secure boot, debug lock, isolated secure code/data regions, and encrypted or integrity-protected persistent storage before production secret storage is enabled.
review_requirements: Provide a local portrait touch display large enough to show raw event kind, signer author or credential identity, complete content or operation summary, complete tags or policy-relevant metadata, request id, approval_digest, and approval status when used as an nSealr signer.
Provide two high side physical buttons with distinct tactile actions for approve/reject or confirmation/cancel.

Require explicit physical approval for signing, credential registration, credential assertion, firmware trust changes, key export, pairing-key changes, secure-element lock changes, and policy changes unless a later device-approved scoped automation policy explicitly accepts the operation.
Reject signing or credential operations when the displayed request id does not match the pending request.
Reject signing or credential operations when the displayed approval_digest does not match the pending request review.
Do not treat touch-only controls, companion UI, NFC tap alone, or host software prompts as final approve or reject consent for production security-device claims.
identity_policy_requirements: This board is the hardware reference platform for custom hardware development in the repo.
When used as an nSealr persistent signer, it must reference the shared nsealr-account-descriptor-v0 route custom_hardware_wallet and custody custom_hardware_persistent.
When used as a USB/NIP-46 class device, it must preserve the policy-manual-only-persistent-device default.

When used for FIDO2/passkey, PKCS#11, HSM, IoT identity, or research firmware, those applications must define their own operation review, key export, debug, and transport policies rather than inheriting nSealr signing assumptions.
Account descriptors, route metadata, FIDO metadata, and companion configuration must remain secretless.
layout_requirements: Use at least a 4-layer PCB with a continuous ground reference under USB, TROPIC01, host MCU, display SPI, NFC controller, power-path, and secure-element SPI.
Use a portrait smartphone-like board outline matched to the touch display envelope, with USB-C receptacle on the bottom short edge and NFC antenna zone on the top short edge.
Place the two side buttons high on the left and right long edges so the device can be used vertically by default while firmware may still support horizontal UI modes.
Place STM32U5, TROPIC01, and OPTIGA as a compact secure island away from USB connector stress, NFC antenna, battery connector, and switching regulators.
Route TROPIC01 SPI short, referenced to uninterrupted ground, with no shared display traffic on the same physical bus.
Put SWD, BOOT, reset, UART, provisioning, power rail, USB, and TROPIC01 pogo test pads where a fixture can reach them without increasing end-user enclosure size.
component_selection_requirements: Use current recommended or vendor-confirmed TROPIC01 parts, not deprecated T101/T103-era assumptions.
Use STM32U585VIT6 LQFP100 as the Rev A0 primary MCU candidate and STM32U575VIT6 LQFP100 as fallback.
Select the EastRising ER-TFT024IPS-3 240x320 ST7789V and FT6336 single-FFC touch panel unless a better documented panel is selected before schematic freeze.
Use GCT USB4105-GF-A as the female USB-C receptacle.
Use an OPTIGA Trust M class second secure element over I2C.
Use ST25R3916B NFC controller with a real tuned antenna path, not decorative antenna graphics.
notes: This is the single custom hardware product direction for TROPIC01 universal secure-device development.
The board is USB connected and battery-capable; it must not claim air gap.
BLE, WiFi, and radio modules are excluded from Rev A0.
microSD is excluded from the single product.
